major_issues: Mobile: the top control row (tabs + Fit/zoom/reset) overflows horizontally and becomes cramped; tap targets are small and the row feels like a desktop toolbar forced into a narrow width.
Mobile: the flow/graph viewport is not prioritized; it consumes space while still being hard to read, with no clear affordance to expand/fullscreen or navigate.
Readability: several secondary labels (timestamps, tiny status text inside nodes, pill metadata) are too small/low-contrast against the dark/blurred background, especially on mobile.
Information hierarchy: right-hand (desktop) / stacked (mobile) panels are dense and similarly styled; primary KPIs (Capital, Runtime state) don’t stand out enough vs long descriptive blocks.
Event strip at the bottom of the flow panel is visually busy and looks like it can clip/overflow; it’s difficult to scan and competes with core content.
medium_issues: Excessive vertical padding between mobile cards increases scroll length; key status requires too much scrolling to reach.
Long strings (URLs, hostnames, tags like agave_preflight_not_green) risk overflow; truncation/ellipsis is inconsistent across chips and headings.
Contrast and focus: many containers use similar dark shades and soft borders; sections blend together and lose separation at a glance.
Buttons 'UI review running' and 'Run UI review loop' sit awkwardly under the header on mobile; alignment and spacing feel unstructured.
Zoom percentage control is not clearly labeled/understood on mobile; plus/minus/reset cluster lacks explanatory tooltip/label and is easy to mis-tap.
minor_issues: Typography scale: header area uses mixed sizes/weights; small monospace system line under the title is tight and slightly noisy.
Inconsistent capitalization/label styling in cards (e.g., section headers vs pill text).
Some cards have large empty areas or overly tall minimum heights, reducing density efficiency.
Node labels in the graph appear close to grid lines; subtle background grid adds noise without strong utility at small sizes.

recommended_changes.change: Add a mobile-specific toolbar layout: wrap controls to 2 lines and increase tap targets (min-height: 40-44px). Use a horizontal scroll only as fallback (overflow-x:auto) with visible spacing; avoid cramming tabs+zoom into one row at <420px.

Increase base font-size on mobile for secondary text and improve contrast: bump small labels to 12–13px minimum, raise muted text color (e.g., from ~#7a to ~#9aa) and reduce blur/opacity behind text blocks.

Implement robust truncation for long strings: apply `max-width:100%`, `overflow:hidden`, `text-overflow:ellipsis`, `white-space:nowrap` to pills/chips/card headers; add `word-break:break-word` for paragraph URLs where wrapping is preferred.

Improve hierarchy in the side panel cards: make KPI cards (Capital/Runtime) visually primary (larger number, stronger border/accent, tighter copy) and reduce prominence of descriptive paragraphs (smaller, more muted, with max width/line-height).
Add a 'Fullscreen / Expand flow' affordance on mobile (and desktop): a button that toggles a class on the flow container to take full viewport height/width and hide side panels while active.
Reduce mobile card spacing and unnecessary min-heights: tighten vertical gaps (e.g., 12–16px), reduce large padding in card bodies, and ensure cards shrink-wrap content to improve density.
Rework the event strip: limit to 1 line with horizontal scroll + fade mask, or show 3–5 most recent items with clear separators. Prevent clipping with `overflow:hidden` and consistent line-height.
Dial back background grid/noise on small screens (lower opacity or disable under a breakpoint) to improve perceived sharpness of nodes and labels.
Add accessible labels/title attributes for icon-only controls (zoom +/-/reset, collapse chevron) and ensure focus styles are visible for keyboard navigation.

stop_reason: Not production-worthy yet due to mobile control overflow/cramped toolbar, weak text readability/contrast for secondary information, and insufficient hierarchy/density tuning across stacked cards.
